note_en: 把 moves the object in front of the verb, and 进去 after the verb shows direction — "in, into it": 千万别把积蓄都投进去 "whatever you do, don't put all your savings into it." 把 is needed when something happens to the object and the result matters: 把手指从确认键上拿开 "took his finger off the Confirm button." In English the object follows the verb; in a Chinese 把 sentence it comes before it.
